label: compiled
paradigm: Match the watch to how this buyer actually uses a second time zone and to their wrist, then get the most watch for the money they set. Heritage, brand and reviewers' enthusiasm inform the choice but never outrank use, fit and verified value. The stance is opportunistic in finding unique pieces that justify their inclusion by value proposition given their distinctiveness.

change_log.reason: imported from formalized-reasoner compile "rank, explain and present a shortlist of new GMT watches for one US buyer's brief (second-zone use, budget or ceiling, wrist, tastes), from a cited basis of watch records, so that the page is coherent with the owner's paradigm and desiderata" (freeze f159884)

spec_fields.gmt_type: string: 'caller' (office: the 24-hour hand is set on its own) or 'flyer' (traveller: the local hour hand jumps in hour steps); unknown if the source does not settle it
spec_fields.warranty_years: number: the maker's warranty in years for a new watch bought in the US
spec_fields.water_resistance_m: number: rated water resistance in metres

wearer.statement: Top three are at or under budget; any stretch is <= 30% over the budget, labelled with the dollar amount over; prices straddling the line are labelled indistinguishable rather than in or out. Alternative considered: judging stretch acceptability holistically; rejected because the cap, amount label and straddle rule are arithmetic on price_usd and the brief.

Each stretch pick carries a reason grounded in use fit, build or distinctiveness that a reader would accept as worth the extra money. Alternative considered: treating any non-empty 'why' as sufficient (static); rejected because whether the reason actually justifies the overrun is value-laden.

Lug-to-lug is compared with the buyer's flat-wrist width via fit(): <= width - 2 mm fits, within +-2 mm is indistinguishable with a try-on advisory, > width + 2 mm is misfit and excluded from ranks; thickness is within the buyer's limit (default 14 mm). Alternative considered: a general 'wearability' concept including taste in size; rejected because the band rule is mechanical and taste belongs to taste_honouring.

No ranked watch carries a must_not style; stated preferences (mechanical, display back, preferred brands) are applied rather than overridden, and any price of honouring them is recorded on the page. Alternative considered: a judged concept; rejected for the exclusion and preference application, which assess() checks, leaving tone of the trade-off to rationale_adjacency.

watch.statement: Every ranked watch is a true 24-hour second-zone GMT (gmt_type caller or flyer, not None) and its labelled type matches the record's type and the buyer's use both ways (office -> caller; traveller or both -> flyer). Alternative considered: a single 'GMT correctness' concept folding in date behaviour; rejected because type/use matching is a pure record-vs-brief check while date disclosure is a presence check on the page, and they fail independently.

check.checks_only: only that the watch is a caller or flyer GMT; whether its type matches the buyer's use is judged

watch.statement: Each ranked and worth-knowing watch is buyable new now from the brand or an authorised US dealer (open pre-order with stated delivery window allowed and labelled), and its warranty length is stated. Alternative considered: trusting record fields as of price_date (static); rejected because availability changes after the record date and needs a live reference check.

check.checks_only: only that the maker's warranty is at least one year; current availability and the stated warranty length are judged

watch.statement: Each ranked watch states a ten-year service range with basis (brand price or labelled class estimate, or service_unpriced) and a total_10y range equal to price plus that range; value comparisons use this total. Alternative considered: putting service under value_pick_dominance; kept separate because a page can state costs correctly yet rank badly, and vice versa.

Ranked watches meet the water-resistance floor (50 m, 100 m if the buyer swims), with sapphire crystal and higher water resistance preferred in ordering and an exhibition case back treated as a bonus, never a requirement. Alternative considered: separate concepts for crystal, water and case back; merged because all are record-attribute preferences applied the same way in ranking.

check.checks_only: only the 50 m water-resistance floor; the 100 m floor for swimmers, crystal and case-back preferences are judged

watch.statement: Each distinctiveness or remarkable claim names an accepted kind (an unusual mechanism or layout, a material, documented design history, a small maker, or a limited run) and is supported by its non-interested cited source in substance, not just in form. Alternative considered: a static check that a kind and non-interested URL are present; that presence check lives in source_coverage_and_interest, while whether the claim really is remarkable is contested.

Each ranked watch carries exactly one cited history or context fact that is accurate and genuinely informative. Alternative considered: counting cited facts (static); the count is trivial but accuracy and relevance of the fact need judgement.

pair.statement: No other fitting, in-budget candidate in the record pool beats rank 1 on function and build at lower total ten-year cost (checked by rerunning rank/assess over the pool). Alternative considered: a judged 'best value' opinion; rejected because dominance over the recorded attributes is computable from the pool.

coherence.name: reason_matches_key
coherence.rationale: The reason given for ranking one watch above another must be the thing that actually separates them in the buyer's agreed order of priorities; a true number given with the wrong reason misleads.

coherence.name: extra_buys_hold
coherence.rationale: A watch that costs more than the buyer prefers to spend earns its place by what the extra money buys; each such claim must be true of the two watches it compares.

coherence.name: date_text_matches_type
coherence.rationale: What the page says the date does when local time changes must match the kind of GMT the page says the watch is.

coherence.name: total_is_price_plus_service
coherence.rationale: Value is judged on the price plus the expected cost of servicing over ten years; the stated total must be exactly that sum.

coherence.name: try_on_label_matches_fit
coherence.rationale: A watch that may or may not fit the buyer's wrist carries a 'try it on first' note, and only such a watch does.

coherence.name: order_follows_key
coherence.rationale: Below first place, the shortlist follows the buyer's agreed order of priorities, except where one distinctive watch is deliberately placed.

coherence.name: stretch_amount_matches
coherence.rationale: A watch over the budget is labelled with exactly how much it is over.

coherence.name: rationale_respects_taste
coherence.rationale: The buyer's stated tastes are honoured and never argued away; whether the wording does so is for a reader to judge.

coherence.name: distinctive_pick_earns_place
coherence.rationale: The distinctive watch must read as worth its place and its cost to this buyer; the checks confirm its sourced claim, and a reader judges its appeal.

warrant.source_slice: rank, explain and present a shortlist of new GMT watches for one US buyer's brief (second-zone use, budget or ceiling, wrist, tastes), from a cited basis of watch records, so that the page is coherent with the owner's paradigm and desiderata

not_exported.reason: This is about what the shortlist page tells the buyer (what the date does when local time changes), not about the watch itself, so it cannot be checked here.
This checks that every figure on the shortlist page has a dated source and that the brand's own pages are flagged as such; it applies to the page, not to one watch.
This checks the links cited on the shortlist page; it applies to the page, not to one watch.
This checks that the reasons for each ranking on the shortlist page use only numbers from the watches' records; there is no ranking to check here.
This checks that each ranked watch's reason explains why it sits above the next and below the previous; there is no ranking to check here.
This checks the shortlist page's short list of remarkable watches outside the buyer's brief; it applies to the page, not to one watch.
This checks that each photo on the shortlist page is credited to the brand's or a dealer's page; it applies to the page, not to one watch.
This checks what the shortlist page says when no watch meets every requirement; it applies to the page, not to one watch.

warrant.not_enforced_note: Validated in the compile but not enforced by the plug-in: criteria listed here are judged on the pages, and the plug-in does not yet score coherence factors, which need facts about the buyer.
